block-definition.comment: Makes a new module and puts it in a variable with the given name. The variable then stands for the module in every other block; its watcher shows the settings. oscillator: produces a tone. Settings: wave (saw, square, triangle or sine), frequency (Hz; 261.6 is middle C), control (a module whose signal bends the frequency, in semitones), trigger (a module whose rising signal restarts the wave). filter: lets the low part of a sound through. Settings: cutoff (Hz; sound above it is cut away), resonance (0 to 100 %; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80), input (the module whose sound is filtered), control (a module whose signal moves the cutoff, in semitones). The settings are saved with the project. After loading, a module is rebuilt from them the next time a block uses it.

Changes one setting of an oscillator. Drop the variable holding the oscillator into the first slot. wave: saw, square, triangle or sine frequency: Hz control: the name of a module whose signal bends the frequency, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it trigger: the name of a module whose rising signal restarts the wave, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match: a list of waves, a typed number, or a list of modules. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.

Changes one setting of a filter. Drop the variable holding the filter into the first slot. cutoff: Hz; sound above it is cut away resonance: 0 to 100 %; emphasis at the cutoff, singing on its own above 80 input: the module whose sound is filtered, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it control: the module whose signal moves the cutoff, chosen from the list, or an empty slot to unplug it Choosing a setting changes the value slot to match. Stack several of these blocks to set several settings.
Plugs a module into the speaker so you hear it. Drop the variable holding the module into the slot. An empty slot unplugs the speaker and silences the synth; the stop sign does the same.

Reports a saved set of oscillator settings. Use it with Snap!'s own variable block: set osc1 to (Preset 1) To store an oscillator's current settings here, use the "set preset" block. The values live in this block's definition, so they are saved with the project and can be edited in the block editor.

Copies the settings of an oscillator into the chosen Preset block, replacing what it held. Control and trigger are stored empty. Drop the variable holding the oscillator into the second slot.
